 Tiny Nick's Gambling Picks 10/23
 By Nick Hamaty - October 23, 2026 
 Locks 
 NBA (0.75 Unit) Minnesota Timberwolves -1.5 @ Orlando Magic (-110; Odds via Fanduel): 6:00 PM CT on DAZN-MIN 
 The Wolves dismantling the Heat in Miami on national TV doesn’t appear to have done much to their power rating, even though a few -2’s are starting to show for this game. Ok, fine, the market doesn’t have to be a believer, but those of us who know this Minnesota team and can see the dynamic are believers. What I’m not a believer in is this Orlando squad, which has never lived up to its potential despite several talented pieces, and the Wolves owe them payback for two losses last season.
 That was on display as they were kept at arm’s length by a talented Atlanta team in the opener. The Hawks didn’t even shoot it particularly well, but still rolled up 132 points against a team that is not living up to its previous defensive reputation. If the Wolves didn’t party too hard on South Beach, they should be able to run their offense similarly to Wednesday night, and pull away from the Magic who are still missing a couple of key pieces as well.
 Bonus Bet (0.5 Unit): Minnesota Timberwolves Team Total Over 118.5 (-110; Odds via Fanduel) 
 This can act as both a supplement to, and a hedge against, laying a short number with the Wolves tonight. If the market turns out to be right and the Wolves were to lose a tight one here, I still don’t have faith that Orlando is going to slow them down. They couldn’t contain Atlanta, who is nowhere near the pace-and-space offense the Wolves bring to this game, so I think they keep putting up monster offensive numbers.
 NBA (0.75 Unit) Dallas Mavericks/Indiana Pacers Over 238.5 (-110; Odds via Caesars): 6:00 PM CT on NBA League Pass 
 The styles of these teams, while different, are just so conducive to overs that I’m pretty amazed we aren’t seeing a total in the 240’s tonight. For the Pacers, it means a return to the true up-tempo style that was made so potent by Tyrese Haliburton and was never the same without him. Pushing pace against a Dallas team that has plenty of defensive questions, especially on the perimeter, should create similar production as Wednesday when they opened the season with 123 points.
 But Dallas should be interesting this season, as new coach Dusty May gives every player the green light from any spot on the floor. Have ball, shoot ball is just another form of up-tempo basketball that shortens possessions, and creates run-outs for a team like Indiana that will love to play in transition. Just to illustrate the point, Dallas only put up 38 in the first half on Wednesday and their game still went well over the total, so I see another high-scoring affair here.
 NBA (0.75 Unit) Duncan Robinson Over 2.5 Made Three’s (+100; Odds via Fanduel): 7:00 PM CT on NBA League Pass 
 What did the last shooting guard do to Miami? Oh yeah, he splashed 9 triples on Wednesday night. Ok, so Duncan Robinson is no Anthony Edwards, and is certainly a streakier shooter, but he’s also facing his former team here and has an excellent matchup. I was convinced before Wednesday and am even more so now that Miami is really going to struggle against the three.
 That’s especially going to be the case while the traffic cone that is Klay Thompson continues to start at shooting guard and has to try to defend a player like Robinson. That has disaster written all over it for the Heat tonight, and after Robinson drained 5 of them in Detroit’s opener, I see another big night for him here.
 Bonus Bets (Duncan Robinson Three-Point Escalator; Odds via Fanduel) 
 These alternate numbers for Robinson are just too juicy and attractive to pass up given the situation and matchup.
 0.5 Unit – Over 3.5 Made Three’s (+250) 
 0.25 Unit – Over 4.5 Made Three’s (+560) 
 0.1 Unit – Over 5.5 Made Three’s (+1150) 
 MLB (0.5 Unit) Tampa Bay Rays +0.5 First Five Innings @ Milwaukee Brewers (+100; Odds via Fanduel): 7:00 PM CT on FOX 
 Given that the Rays are up against Jacob Misiorowski here, you’d think the best outcome for this first five bet is a 0-0 tie. But we haven’t seen the best, most dominant version of The Miz in this postseason, giving up three runs in his two starts, with Brewers opponents going 1-1 to this number. And with Tampa making the surprising decision to start Nick Martinez instead of ace Drew Rasmussen, it might actually give the Rays a sneaky advantage here. Martinez throws a ton of changeups, which can give Milwaukee’s bats trouble, and you’d have to think the long layoff since the NLCS will cause some rust. That’s not uncommon in the MLB postseason, so I’ll take the team that’s in a groove right now to keep it competitive early on tonight.

 No degenerates today.
